title: API Design
overview: A well-designed API is the contract between your service and its consumers. Good API design prioritizes clarity, consistency, versioning, and developer experience. REST is the dominant style for web APIs, while GraphQL shines for flexible data fetching, and gRPC excels for internal high-performance service communication.
keyPoints: Use nouns for resources, not verbs — /users not /getUsers
Use HTTP methods semantically: GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE (remove)
Version your API from day one — /v1/users avoids breaking changes
Implement pagination for collection endpoints — avoid returning unbounded lists
Use consistent error response formats with machine-readable error codes

concepts.name: RESTful Design
concepts.description: Representational State Transfer — stateless, resource-based, leverages HTTP methods and status codes. Widely adopted, excellent tooling, self-documenting with OpenAPI/Swagger.

concepts.name: GraphQL
concepts.description: Client specifies exactly which fields it needs. Eliminates over-fetching and under-fetching. Single endpoint. Great for mobile clients and varied consumer needs.

concepts.name: gRPC
concepts.description: Binary protocol over HTTP/2 using Protocol Buffers. Strongly typed, extremely fast, ideal for internal service-to-service communication. Poor browser support.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.description: GET, PUT, DELETE should be idempotent — calling them multiple times has the same effect as once. Use idempotency keys for POST requests that must not be duplicated.

concepts.name: Rate Limiting Headers
concepts.description: Return X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset headers to help clients self-throttle and avoid hitting limits.

tools.name: OpenAPI / Swagger
tools.description: Industry standard for describing REST APIs — enables auto-generated docs, SDKs, and mock servers

tools.name: Postman
tools.description: API testing and documentation platform with collaborative collections

tools.name: GraphQL Playground / Studio
tools.description: Interactive GraphQL schema explorer and query builder for development and testing

tools.name: Insomnia
tools.description: Open-source API client supporting REST, GraphQL, and gRPC with environment variables

tradeoffs: REST is familiar and widely supported but can lead to over-fetching (getting too much data) or under-fetching (requiring multiple requests). GraphQL solves these but adds query complexity and can expose N+1 query vulnerabilities. gRPC is the fastest but requires code generation and HTTP/2, limiting browser usage. Choose based on consumer needs and team familiarity.
interviewTips: Always version your API — discuss URL versioning (/v1/) vs header versioning
Explain idempotency and why it matters for retry logic in distributed systems
Pagination: discuss cursor-based vs offset-based and when each is appropriate
Authentication: API keys for simple cases, OAuth 2.0 / JWT for user-context APIs
